Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for

# Delta A syntax-highlighting pager for git, diff, and grep output. ## Description Delta is a viewer for git and diff output. It provides language syntax highlighting, word-level diff highlighting, side-by-side view, line numbering, themes, and many other features to make code diffs easier to read and understand. ## Get Started Install delta (the package is called "git-delta" in most package managers, but the executable is just `delta`) and add this to your `~/.gitconfig`: ```gitconfig [core] pager = delta [interactive] diffFilter = delta --color-only [delta] navigate = true # use n and N to move between diff sections dark = true # or light = true, or omit for auto-detection [merge] conflictStyle = zdiff3 ``` Or run: ```sh git config --global core.pager delta git config --global interactive.diffFilter 'delta --color-only' git config --global delta.navigate true git config --global merge.conflictStyle zdiff3 ``` ## Features - Language syntax highlighting with the same syntax-highlighting themes as bat - Word-level diff highlighting using a Levenshtein edit inference algorithm - Side-by-side view with line-wrapping - Line numbering - `n` and `N` keybindings to move between files in large diffs, and between diffs in `log -p` views (`--navigate`) - Improved merge conflict display - Improved `git blame` display (syntax highlighting; `--hyperlinks` formats commits as links to hosting provider etc. Supported hosting providers are: GitHub, GitLab, SourceHut, Codeberg) - Syntax-highlights grep output from `rg`, `git grep`, `grep`, etc - Support for Git's `--color-moved` feature - Code can be copied directly from the diff (`-/+` markers are removed by default) - `diff-highlight` and `diff-so-fancy` emulation modes - Commit hashes can be formatted as terminal hyperlinks to the hosting provider page (`--hyperlinks`) - File paths can also be formatted as hyperlinks for opening in your OS - Stylable box/line decorations to draw attention to commit, file and hunk header sections - Style strings (foreground color, background color, font attributes) are supported for >20 stylable elements, using the same color/style language as git - Handles traditional unified diff output in addition to git output - Automatic detection of light/dark terminal background ## Usage Delta has many features and is very customizable. For complete usage information, run: ```sh delta --help ``` Or see the online user manual in the `manual/` directory. ### Basic Usage ```sh # Use delta for git diff git diff | delta # Use delta for git show git show | delta # Use delta for git log -p git log -p | delta # Use delta for git blame git blame FILE | delta # Use delta for grep grep -r PATTERN | delta ``` ### Side-by-side view Enable side-by-side view in your gitconfig: ```gitconfig [delta] side-by-side = true ``` ### Line numbers Enable line numbers in your gitconfig: ```gitconfig [delta] line-numbers = true ``` ### Themes Delta supports many color themes. View available themes with: ```sh delta --show-syntax-themes --dark # or --light ``` Set a theme in your gitconfig: ```gitconfig [delta] syntax-theme = Dracula ``` See `themes.gitconfig` for additional theme examples and presets. ## Configuration Delta is highly customizable through gitconfig. Key configuration options include: - `syntax-theme`: Color theme for syntax highlighting - `side-by-side`: Enable side-by-side view - `line-numbers`: Show line numbers - `navigate`: Enable n/N keybindings to navigate between files - `hyperlinks`: Format commit hashes and file paths as hyperlinks - `dark` or `light`: Set color scheme for light/dark terminal backgrounds And many more. Run `delta --help` for a complete list of options. ## License See LICENSE file. ===

import subprocess, os
def run(args, input_data=b"", env_extra=None):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    e["HOME"]="/tmp/fakehome_nonexist_test"
    e["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"]="/dev/null"
    e["GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM"]="/dev/null"
    e["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    e["COLUMNS"]="80"
    if env_extra: e.update(env_extra)
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=input_data, capture_output=True, env=e, timeout=10)
    return p

def show(label, minus, plus, extra=[]):
    diff = f"""diff --git a/f.txt b/f.txt
index 123..456 100644
--- a/f.txt
+++ b/f.txt
@@ -1,{len(minus)} +1,{len(plus)} @@
""".encode()
    for m in minus:
        diff+=f"-{m}\n".encode()
    for pl in plus:
        diff+=f"+{pl}\n".encode()
    p=run(["--paging","never","--no-gitconfig"]+extra, input_data=diff)
    print(f"=== {label} ===")
    print(repr(p.stdout))
    print()

# word diff cases
show("single word change", ["old line"], ["new line"])
show("identical?", ["same line"], ["same line"])
show("multiple words", ["foo bar baz"], ["foo qux baz"])
show("added word", ["foo baz"], ["foo bar baz"])
show("removed word", ["foo bar baz"], ["foo baz"])
show("no pairing? multiple minus vs single plus", ["a","b","c"], ["d"])
show("empty minus?", ["foo"], [""])
show("punctuation", ["foo, bar."], ["foo, baz."])
show("long vs short", ["hello world foo bar"], ["hello world"])

import re
# Parse long help for options
with open("/tmp/help_help.txt","rb") as f:
    data=f.read().decode()
# Find option blocks: pattern "      --" or "  -X, --"
# We'll extract via regex on the raw --help text lines that start with spaces + dash
lines=data.splitlines()
opts=[]
for i,line in enumerate(lines):
    m=re.match(r"\s*(-\S, )?(--[\w-]+)(?:\s+<([^>]+)>)?\s*$", line.rstrip())
    # Actually option lines in long help are alone: e.g. "      --blame-code-style <STYLE>"
    # The next lines are description. So match lines that look like option declaration
    if m and line.startswith(" ") and "--" in line:
        # check that line stripped starts with - 
        stripped=line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith("-"):
            # This is an option line
            short=None
            long=None
            val=None
            # parse
            mm=re.match(r"(?:(-\S),\s+)?(--[\S]+)(?:\s+<([^>]+)>)?", stripped)
            if mm:
                short=mm.group(1)
                long=mm.group(2)
                val=mm.group(3)
                # look ahead for possible values/default in next ~10 lines?
                # For now just record
                opts.append((short,long,val,line))
print(f"found {len(opts)}")
for o in opts:
    print(o)
PY

0 # Environment variables ## Git environment variables The `GIT_PAGER` environment variable must either not be set at all, or set to the value `delta` (you can add argument here if you want; this env var plays the same role as the `core.pager` config entry). ## Pager environment variables A pager is a program that accepts many lines of text as input, and displays them one screenful at a time. The standard pager is [less](https://linux.die.net/man/1/less), and this is what delta uses by default (it's also what [`bat`](https://github.com/sharkdp/bat) uses). Therefore: 1. It is very important that you are using a recent version of less. In particular, on Windows, the installed version of less is often broken and it is usually necessary to install it yourself or use the version of less that is installed with git on Windows. 2. The command line flags passed to `less` are important, and there are some environment variables that affect these (see below). By default, delta will try to ensure that they are sensible. 3. When delta is displaying lengthy output, anything you do with the keyboard or mouse is actually received by less, and it is worth looking at less documentation (`less --help` or `man less` or [online](https://linux.die.net/man/1/less)) to discover what you can do. The exact command that `delta` uses to start its pager is taken from one of the following environment variables (in this order): - `DELTA_PAGER` - `BAT_PAGER` - `PAGER` Delta does not use `bat` when it is running, and delta users do not need to install bat. (Delta does use the `bat` Rust library for its syntax highlighting themes and language definitions, and for launching the pager, which is why the `BAT_PAGER` environment variable is honored). If none of these is set, delta uses `less -R`, and you should always include `-R` if you are setting these environment variables yourself. In addition to those `*PAGER` environment variables, the behavior of `less` is also affected by the `LESS` environment variable (see `man less` or [online documentation](https://linux.die.net/man/1/less)). This env var can contain command line options and/or interactive less-commands (prefixed by a leading `+` sign; these are executed every time right after less is launched). ## Delta-specific environment variables To temporarily activate and inactivate delta features, you can use `DELTA_FEATURES`, e.g. ```sh export DELTA_FEATURES='+side-by-side my-feature' ``` (The `+` means "add these features to those configured in git config".) The `DELTA_PAGER` env var is described above. # "Features": named groups of settings All delta options can go under the `[delta]` section in your git config file. However, you can also use named "features" to keep things organized: these are sections in git config like `[delta "my-feature"]`. Here's an example using two custom features: ```gitconfig [delta] features = unobtrusive-line-numbers decorations whitespace-error-style = 22 reverse [delta "unobtrusive-line-numbers"] line-numbers = true line-numbers-minus-style = "#444444" line-numbers-zero-style = "#444444" line-numbers-plus-style = "#444444" line-numbers-left-format = "{nm:>4}┊" line-numbers-right-format = "{np:>4}│" line-numbers-left-style = blue line-numbers-right-style = blue [delta "decorations"] commit-decoration-style = bold yellow box ul file-style = bold yellow ul file-decoration-style = none hunk-header-decoration-style = yellow box ```
The environment variable `DELTA_FEATURES` can used to enable features from the command line: it should be set to a space-separated string of feature names. If you precede this with a `+` symbol, then the features are _added_ to those configured elsewhere, instead of replacing them. This is very useful, for example to temporarily switch delta to side-by-side mode you can do ```sh export DELTA_FEATURES=+side-by-side ``` and to undo that: ```sh export DELTA_FEATURES=+ ```

import subprocess, os
def run(args, input_data=b"", env_extra=None):
    e=dict(os.environ)
    e["HOME"]="/tmp/fakehome_nonexist_test"
    e["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"]="/dev/null"
    e["GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM"]="/dev/null"
    e["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    e["COLUMNS"]="80"
    if env_extra: e.update(env_extra)
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, input=input_data, capture_output=True, env=e, timeout=15)
    return p

caps=[
    (["--help"], "help_long.bin", b""),
    (["-h"], "help_short.bin", b""),
    (["--version"], "version.bin", b""),
    (["-V"], "version2.bin", b""),
    (["--generate-completion","bash"], "comp_bash.bin", b""),
    (["--generate-completion","fish"], "comp_fish.bin", b""),
    (["--generate-completion","zsh"], "comp_zsh.bin", b""),
    (["--generate-completion","elvish"], "comp_elvish.bin", b""),
    (["--generate-completion","powershell"], "comp_powershell.bin", b""),
    (["--list-syntax-themes"], "list_syntax_themes.bin", b""),
    (["--list-languages"], "list_languages.bin", b""),
    (["--show-syntax-themes"], "show_syntax_dark.bin", b""),
    (["--show-syntax-themes","--light"], "show_syntax_light.bin", b""),
    (["--show-syntax-themes","--dark"], "show_syntax_dark2.bin", b""),
    (["--show-colors"], "show_colors.bin", b""),
    (["--show-config"], "show_config.bin", b""),
    (["--show-config","--light"], "show_config_light.bin", b""),
    (["--show-config","--dark"], "show_config_dark.bin", b""),
]
for args, fn, inp in caps:
    p=run(args, input_data=inp)
    open(f"/tmp/captures/{fn}","wb").write(p.stdout)
    print(f"{args} -> {fn} len={len(p.stdout)} err={len(p.stderr)} exit={p.returncode}")
    if p.stderr:
        print("  stderr:", repr(p.stderr[:200]))

# also capture show-themes error
p=run(["--show-themes"])
print(f"show-themes exit={p.returncode} out={len(p.stdout)} err={repr(p.stderr[:500])}")
open("/tmp/captures/show_themes_err.bin","wb").write(p.stderr)

# capture help error variants? Not needed
PY
ls -lh /tmp/captures/
"}

# Usage

The main way to use delta is to configure it as the pager for git: see [Configuration](./configuration.md).

Delta can also be used as a shorthand for diffing two files, even if they are not in a git repo: the following two commands do the same thing:

```sh
delta /somewhere/a.txt /somewhere/else/b.txt

git diff /somewhere/a.txt /somewhere/else/b.txt
```

You can also use [process substitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Process_substitution) shell syntax with delta, e.g.

```sh
delta <(sort file1) <(sort file2)
```

In addition to git output, delta handles standard unified diff format, e.g. `diff -u a.txt b.txt | delta`.

For Mercurial, you can add delta, with its command line options, to the `[pager]` section of `.hgrc`.

    cmd=""
    opts=""

    for i in ${COMP_WORDS[@]}

        case "${cmd},${i}" in

                cmd="delta"
                ;;
            *)
                ;;
        esac
    done

    out = f"{BOLD}{RED}error:{RESET} a value is required for '{YELLOW}{long} <{valname}>{RESET}' but none was supplied\n"

    out = f"{BOLD}{RED}error:{RESET} invalid value '{YELLOW}{val}{RESET}' for '{BOLD}{long} <{valname}>{RESET}'"
    if reason:
        out += f": {reason}"
    out += "\n"
    if possible:

        out += f"  [possible values: {plist}]\n"
    out += f"\nFor more information, try '{BOLD}--help{RESET}'.\n"
    return out

            d = open(p,"rb").read().decode()
            return d
        except:
